page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-highmem-96-metal is a bare-metal server configured with 96 dedicated vCPUs based on the 64-bit Arm (arm64) architecture. The platform includes 768.0 GB of system memory, establishing a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The server contains no graphic processing units (GPUs) and provides no bundled local disk storage.

Because the system runs directly on bare metal with dedicated core allocation, workloads operate without hypervisor overhead. The high memory density accommodates substantial working sets in system RAM. However, the absence of integrated local storage means all file system structures and persistent data layers rely on attached network storage. In addition, no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned to the instance.

From a resource utilization standpoint, the combination of energy-efficient Arm architecture and high memory capacity enables cost-effective scaling for applications where memory constraints dominate. GCP c4a-highmem-96-metal is best matched for large in-memory databases, distributed caching layers, memory-bound enterprise software, and large-scale data analytics pipelines tailored for Arm64 environments.
